title: Every Sky Primitive is instrumented with a Hub Document that indexes its Instances by lifecycle status
content:
Across A.6.1.1.2.2.1.1.1, A.6.1.1.2.2.1.2.1, A.6.1.1.2.2.1.3.1, A.6.1.1.2.2.1.4.1 and A.6.1.1.2.2.2.1.1, the same skeleton repeats verbatim for every Primitive Grove uses: a **Primitive Hub Document** that "organize[s] all base information relevant to Grove's usage" of that Primitive, containing a Global Activation Status, an Active Instances Directory, a Completed Instances Directory, an In Progress Invocations Directory, and a Hub Data Repository whose subtrees hold **Failed Invocations** and **Suspended Instances**.

The repetition is the point. A reader who learns the skeleton once can navigate any Primitive in any Agent Artifact without re-learning its layout, and a reviewer can ask the same five questions of every Primitive: is it on, what is running, what finished, what is being attempted, and what went wrong.

The inclusion of failure and suspension as *first-class locations* rather than exceptional cases is the strongest signal here. Failed Invocations are not deleted; they are archived to a defined address. The structure therefore enforces retention of negative history, which is what makes the process auditable rather than merely documented.

The cost is verbosity: most of these directories are empty stubs, which is why Agent Artifacts run to enormous length with low information density per section.
description: Active, Completed and In Progress directories plus a Hub Data Repository holding failed Invocations and Suspended Instances give each Primitive a uniform, externally auditable state machine.
